newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says two dead in Israeli army raid.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says two dead in Israeli army raid.

text.p: Israeli troops infiltrated one mile (1.5 km) north of their occupation zone in south Lebanon and killed two Hizbollah guerrillas in a pre-dawn attack, a Hizbollah spokesman said on Tuesday.

The clash occurred at 2.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Monday) between the villages of Froon and Ghandourieh in the central section of the frontline and the two sides fought in the dark with automatic weapons and anti-tank grenades, the spokesman said.
A number of Israelis were believed wounded, he added.
The Israeli army said earlier its soldiers killed two guerrillas and wounded a number of others in the raid.

"At least two terrorists were killed and a number were wounded when an army force working north of the security zone in the area of the village Ghandouriyeh hit a terrorist unit of the Hizbollah. There are no Israeli casualties," the army said in a statement issued in Jerusalem.
Israel's army radio and Israel Radio identified the army unit as the Egoz (nut in Hebrew) which is dedicated to search and destroy missions against guerrillas.
The army said the raid was a lesson to guerrillas they could not act with impunity against Israeli troops and their client South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.

"The hit against the terrorists in the outskirts of the villages used as launching bases for operations against the army and SLA clarifies the army will not allow terrorist operations in the villages and their environs, something that contradicts the Grapes of Wrath understandings," the army statement said.
On Sunday, one SLA man was killed and two others were wounded by a roadside bomb Hizbollah said its men planted.

Grapes of Wrath was Israel's code name for its blitz against guerrillas in Lebanon a year ago that killed some 200 Lebanese, most of them civilians. No Israelis were killed though some 50 civilians were wounded by guerrilla rockets launched at northern Israel.
The blitz ended with a U.S. brokered set of understandings barring the sides from firing at or from civilian areas.
